questions.question: The Biraja Temple, the Rajarani Temple and the Samaleswari Temple are all located in ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The **Biraja Temple, the Rajarani Temple** and the **Samaleswari Temple** are all located in **Odisha.**__
 
• __Biraja Temple - __
 __
 
• ​Biraja Temple or **Viraja Kshetra** is one of the ancient Hindu temples located in the **Jajpur district of Odisha, India. **
 
• This present temple was built in the **13th century. **
 
• It is situated in the Jajpur township which is nearly **125 KM north from Bhubaneswar. **
 
• The main idol is **Devi Durga** who is worshipped by the name **Viraja.**
 
 
 
• Rajarani Temple - __
 __
 
• ​The temple was built during the later stages of the **Somavamsi rule in the 11th century AD. **
 
• Today the temple today is **devoid of any presiding deity**, though there are signs in the architecture of the temple to corroborate that it was a temple dedicated to **Lord Shiva.**
 
• The temple is known as Rajarani Temple, because of the **red and yellow sandstone called Rajarania** that was used in its construction. 
 
 
 
• Samaleswari Temple - __
 
 
• The Samaleswari Temple is situated at **Sambalpur, Odisha.**
 
• The abode of Goddess Samaleswari -the presiding deity of Sambalpur is one of the most revered temples of the state. 
 
• Goddess Samaleswari was appropriated as the deity of Sambalpur by the **Chouhan King Balaram Dev**, who became the King of the region in **1542 AD.**
 
• Sambalpur region is popularly known as ***Hirakhanda*** from ancient times.

questions.question: ________ is the largest slum in Asia.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharavi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dharavi** is located in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.
 
• It is considered **one of the largest slums in Asia** and the world.
 
• Dharavi spans over **2.1 square kilometers** and is home to approximately 700,000 to 1,000,000 people.
 
• Despite its poverty, Dharavi is known for its **thriving small-scale industries** such as pottery, textiles, and recycling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slum Definition**

 
 
• A slum is a densely populated urban residential area characterized by substandard housing and squalor.
 
• Slums often lack basic services such as sanitation, clean water, reliable electricity, and adequate living space.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization and Slums**
 
 
• Rapid urbanization often leads to the growth of slums as people migrate to cities in search of better economic opportunities.
 
• Due to high demand and limited supply of affordable housing, many people end up living in informal settlements.
 
 
 
• **Economic Activity in Dharavi**
 
 
• Dharavi is a hub for numerous small-scale industries, generating an estimated annual turnover of over $1 billion USD.
 
• These industries include leather goods, textiles, pottery, and food production, among others.
 
 
 
• **Social and Health Challenges**
 
 
• Residents of slums like Dharavi often face significant health challenges due to poor living conditions.
 
• Common issues include malnutrition, infectious diseases, and lack of access to healthcare services.

• **The Thar Desert,** also referred to as the Great Indian Desert,** lies to the northwest of the Aravalli Range**, a mountain range extending from **Delhi to Gujarat **in northwest India.
 
• It comprises an undulating sandy plain adorned with sand dunes, serving as a natural demarcation between **India and Pakistan**.
 
• Acting as a barrier, the Aravalli Range obstructs moisture-laden winds from reaching the Thar Desert, resulting in arid conditions due to the rain shadow effect caused by the range.
 
• Ranked as the world's 18th-largest desert and the 9th-largest hot subtropical desert, the Thar Desert spans an area of 200,000 square kilometers (77,000 square miles) across India and Pakistan.
 
• Approximately 85% of the desert falls within India's borders, with the remaining 15% located in Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png]

• A considerable portion of the desert landscape is characterized by expansive, shifting sand dunes that accumulate sediments from the adjacent alluvial plains and coastline.
 
• These sand dunes exhibit high mobility, driven by the powerful winds that intensify annually before the arrival of the monsoon season.
 
• Within the desert, the Luni River stands as the sole watercourse.

questions.question: The beautiful square-shaped Mughal architecture, Kanch Mahal is situated in which of the following cities of India?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• It is known for its large-scale use of marble, intricate carvings, and symmetrical designs.

• He was known for his interest in art, architecture, and nature.
 
• Jahangir's era saw the construction of many significant buildings and gardens.

questions.question: Which of the following mosques/masjids was built during the reign of Lodi dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Moth ki Masjid, Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Moth ki Mosque,** a significant heritage site located in Delhi, was constructed in 1505 by Wazir Miya Bhoiya, who served as the Prime Minister during the reign of Sikander Lodi (1489–1517) of the Lodi dynasty.
 
• This mosque represents a new architectural style developed by the Lodis in the fourth city of medieval Delhi within the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• The name "Moth ki Mosque" translates to "Lentil Mosque" in English.
 
• This unique name carries an intriguing legend. The mosque is renowned for its beautiful dome (Gumbad) structure, characteristic of the period in which it was built.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

__
 
• The Lodī dynasty (1451–1526) marked the final ruling family of the Delhi Sultanate in India and hailed from Afghan descent.
 
• Bahlūl Lodī (reigned 1451–89), the inaugural Lodī ruler, emerged as the most dominant figure among the Punjab chiefs.
 
• He ascended to power by supplanting the last monarch of the Sayyid dynasty in 1451.
 
• Bahlūl's dynamic leadership enabled him to unify a disparate coalition of Afghan and Turkish chiefs, expanding his realm from the vicinity of Delhi to encompass regions bordering Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Begumpur Mosque**, situated in the heart of the sultanate's capital, Jahanpanah, formerly part of south Delhi, was erected during the reign of either Muhammad Shah Tughluq (1325-1351) or his successor, Feroz Shah (reg. 1351-1388).
 
• **The Lal Masjid of Delhi**, also referred to as the Fakr-ul Masjid (meaning "Pride of Mosques") or Sikandar Sahib's Masjid, is located in Bara Bazaar, Kashmiri Gate, Old Delhi, India.
 
• **The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque**, constructed between 1192 and 1316, was sponsored by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the founder of the Mamluk dynasty. This mosque is renowned for its iconic tower of victory, symbolizing the Islamic conquest of India.

questions.question: Amar Jawan Jyoti was installed under the Arch of India Gate in January ______.
questions.solution:

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Amar Jawan Jyoti (Immortal Soldier Flame, or light)** is an Indian memorial conceptualized and constructed after the **Indo-Pakistani War of 1971 and inaugurated on 26 January 1972.**
 
• The war, which lasted from 3 to 16 December 1971, and ended with the Fall of Dhaka, was part of the liberation war in East Pakistan.
 
• On 26 January 1972, the twenty-third Republic Day of India, the monument was officially inaugurated by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• It was the national war memorial in India until February 2019, when the new National War Memorial and its own flame were inaugurated and lit.
 
• On 21 January 2022, the older flame was merged with the newer one at National War Memorial.
 
• **Amar Jawan Jyoti is now located at the inner ring, the Amar Chakra (Circle of Immortality), of the National War Memorial.**
 
• The Memorial has four concentric circles representing a Chakravyuh and a central obelisk at the bottom of which burns the flame.
